analysis.investment_thesis: Icon Facilitators is a tiny INR 41 Cr facilities management microcap with a P/E of 11.1 that looks cheap only because profits are negligible — ROE is a punishing 0.48%, meaning the business barely earns anything on its capital. There's no "story" here: no visible growth engine, no differentiation in a commoditized integrated FM industry dominated by larger players.
key_strengths: High promoter holding of 70.75% signals skin in the game
Low absolute P/E of 11.1 in a generally expensive market
Facilities management industry has secular tailwinds in India
key_risks: ROE of 0.48% is near zero — capital is barely productive
INR 41 Cr market cap = illiquid microcap with execution/disclosure risk
Commoditized industry with thin margins and heavy competition
red_flags: ROE of 0.48% indicates no real earning power despite reported P/E
Negligible institutional interest (DII 0.27%, no FII disclosed)
No visible growth rate data to even compute a PEG
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Lynch GARP lens, this fails the most basic filter: you need growth at a reasonable price, and there's simply no evidence of growth or genuine profitability. ROE of 0.48% tells me the company is earning roughly nothing on shareholder capital — a P/E of 11 on near-zero earnings is a mathematical artifact, not a bargain. Facilities management can be a decent niche (I like boring, observable businesses), but the winners are scaled players like Updater Services or global majors; a 41 Cr shop has no moat, no pricing power, and no operating leverage visible in these numbers.

I'd want to see revenue growth >15%, ROE trending toward 15%+, and a credible client concentration story before touching this. None of that is here. Classify this as a speculative microcap, not a fast-grower or stalwart — and the absence of any growth data means I can't even compute the PEG that would be my deciding metric. Pass; there are far better small-cap stories in India with actual earnings power.
